statements.text: For ocular-pressure reduction, bimatoprost is described in the current LUMIGAN label as a prostaglandin analog and synthetic structural analog that mimics prostamide activity; it lowers intraocular pressure by increasing outflow through both trabecular meshwork and uveoscleral pathways.
For eyelash growth, the precise mechanism is unknown; LATISSE is believed to increase the percentage of follicles in anagen and the duration of the growth phase.
After ocular administration, intraocular-pressure reduction begins approximately 4 hours after the first dose and reaches maximum effect at about 8 to 12 hours.
Once-daily ocular LUMIGAN reduces elevated intraocular pressure in open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension.
Once-daily LATISSE applied to the upper eyelid margin increases eyelash prominence, including growth, length, thickness, and darkness.
Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure in patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension.
Treatment of eyelash hypotrichosis by increasing eyelash growth, length, thickness, and darkness.
The most common LUMIGAN reaction is conjunctival hyperemia; ocular pruritus, irritation, dry eye, eyelash growth, and periocular pigmentation can also occur.
Most common LATISSE reactions are ocular pruritus, conjunctival hyperemia, skin hyperpigmentation, ocular irritation, dry-eye symptoms, and erythema of the eyelid.
Clinically important ocular risks include likely permanent iris pigmentation, intraocular inflammation, macular edema in susceptible eyes, and contamination-associated bacterial keratitis.
statements.scope: Product-specific warnings combined only where both labels support the risk

statements.text: Prostaglandin-associated periorbitopathy, including deepening of the eyelid sulcus and other periocular changes, has been reported with ophthalmic use.
Adverse effects are mainly ocular and periocular: hyperemia, irritation, pigment changes, eyelash or hair growth, inflammatory complications, and contamination-related infection.
Neither the current LUMIGAN nor LATISSE label contains a boxed warning; important ocular and periocular risks are described under Warnings and Precautions.
Both reviewed products are contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to bimatoprost or any ingredient.

Iris pigmentation is likely to be permanent; periorbital pigmentation and eyelash changes have been reported to reverse in some patients after discontinuation, and the long-term effects of increased pigmentation are unknown.
statements.scope: Do not describe every pigment or periocular change as permanent

statements.text: Use caution in active intraocular inflammation and in patients at risk for macular edema.

Avoid contaminating the LUMIGAN bottle tip; for LATISSE, keep the bottle intact, do not touch the tip to another surface, and use a new sterile single-use applicator for each eye because contamination can cause infection or bacterial keratitis.
LATISSE is applied only to the upper eyelid margin; blot excess solution and avoid lower-lid application to reduce unwanted hair growth outside the treatment area.
LUMIGAN begins lowering intraocular pressure about 4 hours after the first ocular dose.
LUMIGAN is dosed once daily in the evening; more frequent administration can reduce the pressure-lowering effect.

Systemic elimination half-life after intravenous administration in healthy subjects was approximately 45 minutes, but this systemic value does not define the duration of local ocular or eyelash effects.
After ocular exposure, bimatoprost undergoes oxidation, N-deethylation, and glucuronidation; systemic concentrations are low.
More-frequent-than-recommended LUMIGAN dosing can reduce its pressure-lowering effect; separate multiple topical ophthalmic drugs by at least 5 minutes.
Concomitant LATISSE with LUMIGAN or another prostaglandin analog can interfere with the desired intraocular-pressure reduction; use only after clinician review and monitor intraocular pressure.
statements.scope: LATISSE in a patient receiving ocular hypotensive prostaglandin therapy

statements.text: For glaucoma or ocular hypertension, monitor intraocular pressure and ocular inflammation, macular status in susceptible patients, pigmentation, and adherence to once-daily evening dosing.

For eyelash hypotrichosis, monitor ocular symptoms, pigment and eyelid changes, unwanted hair outside the application area, and intraocular pressure when the patient also uses ocular hypotensive therapy.
Human pregnancy data are insufficient to establish risk; use only when the potential benefit justifies potential fetal risk.
It is unknown whether bimatoprost is present in human milk; weigh breastfeeding benefits, maternal need, and potential infant effects.
The reviewed labels do not provide a renal dose adjustment for locally administered bimatoprost; systemic exposure is low but disease-specific monitoring remains appropriate.
No dose adjustment is provided for hepatic impairment in the reviewed local products; systemic pharmacokinetic evidence is limited.
LUMIGAN use is not recommended in patients younger than 16 years because of concern for increased pigmentation after long-term use.
LATISSE safety and effectiveness have not been established in children younger than 5 years.
No overall clinically significant safety or effectiveness differences were observed between elderly and other adult patients in the reviewed labels.
No information is available on overdose in humans; if accidental oral ingestion occurs, monitor and provide symptomatic and supportive treatment.
Bimatoprost lowers intraocular pressure by increasing both trabecular and uveoscleral outflow; classic adverse effects are conjunctival hyperemia, iris/periocular pigmentation, and eyelash growth.
Product distinction: LUMIGAN is instilled into the eye for glaucoma or ocular hypertension, whereas LATISSE is brushed on the upper eyelid margin for eyelash hypotrichosis.
